# Tantivy Native Conversion Gap Analysis

This document records what is running on the Tantivy-native path in
Steelsearch and what remains on fallback or compatibility-layer
execution.

> Current readiness note (2026-05-30): this gap analysis is not a product-completion certificate. The current worktree fails pipefail-checked `cargo check -p os-engine-tantivy` and native test-harness compilation. See [tantivy-native-production-readiness-audit.md](/home/ubuntu/steelsearch/docs/rust-port/tantivy-native-production-readiness-audit.md).

The latest recorded benchmark reference for this snapshot line is:

- [summary.json](/home/ubuntu/steelsearch/target/search-benchmark-matrix-native-reduce-rerun/summary.json)
- [report.md](/home/ubuntu/steelsearch/target/search-benchmark-matrix-native-reduce-rerun/report.md)

## Current benchmark snapshot

Configuration:

- corpus size: `1000`
- duration: `5s`
- clients: `4`
- shards: `3`
- replicas: `1`
- vector dimension: `16`

Headline numbers:

- Steelsearch 1-node: `108.63 ops/s`
- OpenSearch 1-node: `172.94 ops/s`
- Steelsearch 3-node: `109.88 ops/s`
- OpenSearch 3-node: `69.20 ops/s`

Relevant latency snapshot:

- Steelsearch 1-node lexical p95: `40.80ms`
- Steelsearch 1-node sort_filter p95: `41.75ms`
- Steelsearch 1-node facet p95: `43.22ms`
- Steelsearch 3-node sort_filter p95: `41.90ms`

Interpretation:

- the native custom sort collector improved the sorted search path modestly;
- the engine is not fully Tantivy-native end to end;
- the next material gains depend on removing fallback aggregation and search-hit
  materialization overhead, not only on more query rewrites;
- at this snapshot, the remaining gap reads increasingly as broader
  parity/generalization/orchestration backlog rather than a short list of
  isolated representative holes.
- many of the previously local wrapper/admission questions are explicit in
  code and docs, so the higher-payoff next steps are increasingly evidence-
  gated semantics and caller-propagation questions rather than more local scaffolding
  extraction alone.
- the remaining source-backed matcher family now also reads more uniformly at
  the field-lookup layer, including `more_like_this` matched-field recovery,
  so dotted/nested field-addressing drift is less of a separate residual axis.
- the same field-lookup convergence now also covers source-backed plugin
  metric collection and `top_metrics` metric-object projection, so dotted or
  nested field-addressing drift is less likely to persist in those
  aggregation-side fallback surfaces either.
- the same aggregation-side field-lookup convergence now also covers
  diversified-sampler source-key extraction, so dotted/nested field-addressing
  drift is less likely to survive in that sampled-collection gate either.
- the same aggregation-side field-lookup convergence now also covers
  source-backed `terms`, `range`, `date_histogram`, `histogram`, `missing`,
  `cardinality`, and composite-key collection paths, so dotted/nested field-
  addressing drift is less likely to persist in those fallback bucket/metric
  collectors either.
- the same field-path convergence now also reaches mapped field ingestion,
  visible-field byte estimation, and plugin `auto_date_histogram` /
  `variable_width_histogram` interval selection, so dotted/nested field
  addressing is less likely to fork between indexing-side and aggregation-side
  helper surfaces either.
- the remaining top-level builder fallbacks now read increasingly as explicit
  Tantivy-surface boundaries rather than local uncertainty: current local
  Tantivy 0.21.1 still exposes no nested-query primitive, no geo-distance
  query primitive, no plain `Query` seat for KNN, and no direct aggregation
  request variants for `weighted_avg`, `boxplot`, `extended_stats`,
  `percentile_ranks`, `median_absolute_deviation`, or `cardinality`.
- the shared `source_value_for_highlight_field(...)` lookup now also takes the
  plain no-dot field fast path directly while preserving dotted-path behavior,
  so the now-broader source-backed matcher/evidence/aggregation family shares
  the same cheaper common lookup seat for scalar field names.
- the pipeline bucket-value path is also one layer thinner now: the one-use
  `bucket_selector_source_value(...)` alias is gone, and the moving/bucket-
  selector family reads straight through `bucket_normalize_source_value(...)`.
- the hit-backed plugin `ip_range` / `date_range` / `geo_distance` seats are
  likewise one layer thinner now: their one-use hit-wrapper helpers are gone,
  and the callers bind directly to the shared `*_from_values(...)` collectors.
- the pipeline metric family is also one layer thinner now: one-use
  `cumulative_sum_pipeline_value(...)` and `derivative_pipeline_value(...)`
  wrappers are gone, and their callers now bind directly to
  `sum_bucket_pipeline_value(...)` and `serial_diff_pipeline_value(..., 1)`.
- the adjacent single-use `avg_bucket_pipeline_value(...)`,
  `min_bucket_pipeline_value(...)`, and `max_bucket_pipeline_value(...)`
  helpers are likewise gone now, and their callers compute directly from
  `bucket_metric_values(...)`.
- the plugin global/sampler doc-count surface is also one layer thinner now:
  one-use `plugin_global_doc_count_surface(...)` and
  `plugin_sampler_doc_count_surface(...)` wrappers are gone, and the callers
  bind directly to `plugin_*_aggregation_value(..., None)`.
- the span containment family is also one layer thinner now: the pure
  argument-swap `matches_span_within_query(...)` alias is gone, and the
  remaining callers bind directly to `matches_span_containing_query(...)`
  with swapped child order.
- the diversified sampler field getter is likewise gone now: the two remaining
  callers read `plugin.params["field"]` directly instead of routing through a
  thin `plugin_diversified_sampler_field(...)` alias.
- at this point the remaining tiny helpers in the same local family mostly read
  as shared multi-caller primitives rather than obvious one-use wrappers, so
  helper-side thin-alias cleanup is close to saturated and the next payoff is
  increasingly behavior/orchestration-side rather than one more local syntax pass.
- `nested` explanation output now also surfaces `matched_nested_values`, so the
  source-backed nested seat no longer stops at a plain path-level matched/not-
  matched summary when multiple nested values are involved.
- `more_like_this` explanation output now also surfaces `matched_fields`, so
  its matched-field-only semantics are visible directly in the user-facing
  description instead of staying implicit in the surrounding fallback behavior.
- `terms` and `terms_set` explanation output now also surfaces
  `matched_value_count`, so candidate-value overlap is visible directly instead
  of stopping at a plain matched/not-matched boolean.
- `geo_distance` explanation output now also surfaces
  `actual_distance_meters`, and `distance_feature` explanation output now also
  surfaces `observed_distance` plus `pivot_magnitude`, so those source-backed
  distance seats no longer stop at a boolean-only matched/not-matched summary.
- `rank_feature` explanation output now also surfaces
  `observed_feature_value`, so the current positive numeric/bool gate no longer
  stays implicit behind a boolean-only matched/not-matched summary.
- `distance_feature` and `rank_feature` explanation output now also surfaces
  `matched_value_count`, so array-backed feature overlap is directly visible
  instead of only exposing one observed distance/value seat.
- tokenized `match_phrase`, `match_phrase_prefix`, and `match_bool_prefix`
  explanation output now also surfaces `matched_token_count` plus
  `query_token_count`, so token overlap is directly visible instead of staying
  implicit behind a plain matched/not-matched boolean.
- source-backed `match_phrase`, source-backed `match_phrase_prefix`,
  source-backed `match_bool_prefix`, and source-backed `multi_match` now have
  guarded native builder plus hybrid candidate-reduction evidence for the
  current explicit-field text subsets.
- plain `match` explanation output now also surfaces `matched_value_count`, so
  array-backed source overlap is visible directly instead of collapsing to a
  boolean-only matched/not-matched summary.
- pattern leaf family (`prefix`, `wildcard`, `regexp`, `fuzzy`) explanation
  output now also surfaces `matched_value_count`, so array-backed source
  overlap is visible directly instead of collapsing to a boolean-only
  matched/not-matched summary.
- scalar leaf family (`term`, `range`, `exists`) explanation output now also
  surfaces `matched_value_count`, so array-backed source overlap is visible
  directly instead of collapsing to a boolean-only matched/not-matched
  summary.
- token-AND multi-field family (`combined_fields`, `query_string`,
  `simple_query_string`) explanation output now also surfaces
  `matched_token_count` plus `query_token_count`, so token overlap across
  fields is directly visible instead of staying implicit behind a plain
  matched/not-matched boolean.
- `multi_match` explanation output now also surfaces `matched_value_count`, so
  the current field-OR overlap size is directly visible instead of stopping at
  a matched-field-set summary.
- `more_like_this` explanation output now also surfaces
  `matched_token_count`, so like-token overlap is directly visible instead of
  stopping at a matched-field-set summary.
- `ids` explanation output now also surfaces `matched_value_count`, so exact
  candidate overlap is visible directly instead of stopping at a boolean-only
  matched/not-matched summary.
- `span_containing` and `span_within` explanation output now also surfaces
  `big_match` plus `little_match`, so the two positive-child admission signals
  are visible directly instead of stopping at the outer containment boolean.
- `span_first` explanation output now also surfaces `child_match`, and
  `span_near` explanation output now also surfaces `matched_child_clauses`, so
  those span-family outer summaries no longer stop at a bare `source_match`
  boolean.
- delegate wrapper family (`span_multi`, `field_masking_span`, `wrapper`,
  `constant_score`, `function_score`, `script_score`) now also surfaces
  `source_match` in the outer description, so wrapper-level summaries no
  longer rely on child-detail presence alone.
- `span_not` outer description now also surfaces `source_match`, so the final
  include-without-exclude admission signal is visible directly instead of
  living only in the separate `matched` field.
- `dis_max` and `boosting` outer descriptions now also surface
  `source_match`, so the final combinator admission signal is visible directly
  instead of being inferred from matched-child or positive/negative child
  counts alone.
- `pinned` outer description now also surfaces `source_match`, so the final
  pinned-or-organic admission signal is visible directly instead of being
  inferred from the separate `pinned_match` and `organic_match` fields.
- `bool` outer description now also surfaces `source_match`, so the final
  bool-admission result is visible directly instead of being inferred from the
  aggregate source/highlight/projected match counts alone.
- `span_or` outer description now also surfaces `source_match`, so the final
  any-child admission signal is visible directly instead of being inferred
  from the matched-child count alone.
- `knn` outer description now also surfaces `source_match`, so the final
  vector-shape-plus-filter admission signal is visible directly instead of
  being inferred from vector compatibility and separate filter counts alone.
- `knn` filter detail now also surfaces `filter_match`, so the filter's own
  final admission signal is visible directly instead of being inferred from
  aggregate source/highlight/projected counts alone.
- `span_not` now also exposes a structured `source_match` field alongside the
  legacy `matched` field, so consumers no longer need to infer or rename the
  final admission signal themselves.
- `geo_distance` explanation output now also surfaces `matched_value_count`, so
  array-backed geo-point overlap within the requested distance is visible
  directly instead of only exposing the minimum observed distance.
- multi-index native reduce hint collection now also uses
  `source_value_for_highlight_field(...)` for cardinality value hints, so
  dotted/nested field addressing stays aligned between source-backed hint
  collection and the surrounding aggregation fallback/reduce surface.
- `distance_feature` observed-distance reporting now also uses the same
  recursive array-aware distance helper as the matcher, so array-valued source
  fields no longer drift between explanation output and live match semantics.
- short status summary: most covered lexical/aggregation/sort/hybrid families
  stand as representative-complete with broader backlog remaining, while
  vector work retains structural subsystem blockers even though pure
  `knn`, size=`0` hybrid vector boundaries, and
  hybrid/vector-scored document-backed aggregation collection, and
  single-index vector page-count/aggregation dispatch have narrowed
  further; that short-status shape should stand on the
  broader landed response/materialization surface described
  below rather than as a separate top-of-doc summary note.

This means Steelsearch can execute the main lexical candidate selection,
local tuple sort, and a broad set of bucket/metric aggregation work without
routing every operation back through the source-backed compatibility evaluator.

The plugin-defined `range` landing remains intentionally numeric-only:
it still reuses `RangeBucket { from/to: f64 }` parsing plus `Value::as_f64()`
bucket matching on the collection side. Nearby plugin-defined `ip_range`,
`date_range`, and `geo_distance` now stand on their own source-backed
parser/matcher carriers instead of pretending to be one-line aliases of that
numeric path, so the code keeps the numeric `RangeBucket { from/to: f64 }`
plus `Value::as_f64()` boundary explicit while the IP/date/geo sibling seats
use their own parse/match carriers.

For native aggregation families that do not need fetch-phase hit payloads,
Steelsearch computes against native document sets instead of materializing
full `SearchHit` structures first.

For single-index `size=0` searches whose aggregations are fully native and do
not require vector scoring, Steelsearch skips top-level hit fetch entirely
and returns count plus aggregation results directly.

For single-index searches with no aggregations, no vector scoring, and native
  fast-field sort coverage, Steelsearch executes a native paginated fetch
path that counts total hits separately and materializes only the requested page
of returned hits instead of building `SearchHit` values for every match first.

For single-index lexical searches with no aggregations and no vector scoring,
Steelsearch uses the native page-fetch strategy for unsorted result
sets too, counting total hits separately and materializing only the requested
page instead of building `SearchHit` values for every match first.

For single-index vector and direct-path hybrid searches with no
aggregations and default score ordering, Steelsearch computes the
requested page directly instead of materializing the full matched hit list
before pagination.

For direct-path hybrid searches with explicit sort, Steelsearch
keeps only the requested page window instead of materializing the full
matched hit list before sort pagination.

The direct-path hybrid coverage includes representative bool shapes
with `knn` in `should`, `must`, `filter`, and `must_not`, plus lexical
`must_not` clauses and nested bool clauses, including nested lexical
`must_not`, nested `knn must_not`, nested `filter`, including lexical-only `must_not`
and nested lexical-only `must_not`, plus nested optional `should(knn)` with
`minimum_should_match = 0`, nested `minimum_should_match > 1`, and nested bool
shapes with explicit sort; nested `_id` lexical leaf candidates are
representatively covered, and nested scalar/text lexical leaf candidates such
as `match_all`, `match_none`, `exists`, `term`, `terms`, `range`, `match`, `prefix`, and `wildcard`
(including case-insensitive `prefix` / `wildcard` forms and explicit-sort
shapes for `match_all` / `match_none` / `exists` / `term` / `terms` / `range` / `match` / `prefix` / `wildcard`, including nested `exists(service)` explicit `_id asc` / `_id desc`, text/scalar case-insensitive sort variants, case-insensitive text `prefix` / `wildcard` sort variants, multi-value `terms` forms, and typed integer / float / date `range` forms) are
representatively covered, including array-valued source semantics, when there is
a positive candidate source or when `must_not` is the only clause family
present, including nested scalar/text `exists` shapes over fields such as
`service`, `notes`, and `body`, including explicit-sort `exists(service)`
  and `exists(body)` forms, plus scalar/text/array-valued representative
  unsorted and explicit-sort pairs for scalar `term(service)` / `terms(priority)`,
  typed integer/float/date `range` forms, keyword/text `prefix` / `wildcard`
  forms (including case-sensitive and case-insensitive unsorted / sort variants), array-valued
  `term(tags)` / `terms(tags)` / `match(tags)`, and text `term(body)` /
  `match(body)` / `terms(...)` forms,
that preserve lexical-only candidates
alongside `knn`, and includes lexical candidate-reduction
leaves such as `ids` in addition to the existing compatibility `wildcard`
coverage; `_id`-family lexical leaves such as `term`, `terms`, `match`, `ids`, and
`exists`, `prefix`, and `wildcard` build candidate sets directly instead of materializing
native `SearchHit` values first, and native lexical leaves that have a
direct path include representative case-insensitive explicit-sort `prefix`
and `wildcard` shapes in nested lexical-plus-vector forms over both text and

`_id exists`, `_id term`, `_id terms`, `_id match`, `_id prefix`, and `_id wildcard`,
including case-sensitive and case-insensitive `_id prefix` /
`_id wildcard` unsorted and sort shapes across the representative leaf set,

`_id terms`, nested `_id match`, nested `_id prefix`, and nested
case-sensitive / case-insensitive `_id wildcard`
explicit-sort lexical-plus-vector forms,
with those representative `_id prefix` / `_id wildcard` forms pinning the
vector-native paginated fetch phase directly;
document-set path generally reuse that candidate-set path instead of first
building native `SearchHit` values; visible `term`, `terms`, `match`, and

For multi-index lexical searches with no aggregations and no vector scoring,
Steelsearch performs a native per-index page fetch plus native merge
for both sorted and unsorted result sets, materializing only the requested
global page instead of every matching hit across all selected indices first.

For pure `knn` searches and for hybrid `bool` queries that fit the
direct candidate-reduced path, Steelsearch uses native paginated fetch
handling for both single-index and multi-index result pages instead of routing
those requests through the generic full-hit search path first.

For single-index vector and direct-path hybrid searches whose aggregations stay
on the native aggregation path, Steelsearch supports a native
page-fetch plus native aggregation-collection path instead of forcing those
requests back through the generic full-hit aggregation path.

For multi-index searches whose aggregations stay inside the mergeable native
subset and do not require vector scoring, Steelsearch supports a
native page-fetch plus native aggregation-reduce path that returns both the
requested hit page and merged aggregation results without falling back to
top-level all-hit materialization.

For multi-index vector and direct-path hybrid searches whose aggregations
stay inside the mergeable native subset, Steelsearch supports the
native page-fetch plus native aggregation-reduce path instead of forcing
those requests back through the generic full-hit aggregation path.

For single-index searches whose aggregations stay on the native aggregation
path and do not require vector scoring, Steelsearch supports a native
page-fetch plus native aggregation-collection path for `size > 0`, returning
only the requested hit page together with native aggregation results instead of
materializing every matching hit first.

For general searches, Steelsearch defers `MatchAll`-style `all_hits`
materialization until aggregation fallback actually needs it. Queries with no
aggregations, or single-index searches satisfied by native aggregation paths,
no longer pay that extra full-hit scan by default.

## Not native yet

The remaining non-native areas are the actual conversion backlog, but for the
covered representative families that backlog skews more toward
broader parity/generalization/orchestration breadth than toward isolated
basic execution holes.

### 1. Date field execution is incomplete

Current state:

- date fields use Tantivy date fields rather than string-backed text fields;
- native date sort is available for fast-field-backed date columns;
- native date range execution is available for RFC3339 strings and
  `epoch_millis` numeric bounds;
- native `date_histogram` aggregation is available for `minute`, `hour`, `day`,
  `week`, `month`, and `year` interval requests.

Impact:

- remaining date work is mostly parity rather than basic execution
  capability.
- note: no specific representative-sized hole is
  called out inside the covered date families; date work is
  primarily broader parity/path-shape breadth beyond the
  representative set.

### 3. Vector execution is only partially native

Summary: top-level `knn` retrieval and pure `knn` document/count paths are
partially native today, but the vector subsystem has structural
native-conversion blockers rather than only representative-breadth cleanup
work.

Current state:

- top-level `knn` queries use the engine direct vector path instead of
  rescoring every refreshed document through the generic compatibility search
  loop
- unconstrained `knn` requests use the native HNSW candidate path directly
- constrained `knn` requests (`filter`, `min_score`, `max_distance`) use native
  exact vector candidates plus post-filtering instead of full document
  rescoring
- pure `knn` document collect/count paths reuse
  `vector_candidates_for_knn(...)` instead of immediately falling back to
  `score_document_query(...)`-driven refreshed-document scans;
- size=`0` hybrid vector page-count paths reuse the reduced-
  candidate hybrid page path before falling back to broader
  `count_documents_for_query(...)` scanning;
- hybrid/vector-scored document-backed aggregation collection
  first tries an index-aware reduced-candidate path
  (`collect_aggregations_native_index_aware_with_context(...)` together with
  `search_documents_for_query_index_aware(...)`), and the
  vector-native page+aggregation path uses that direct with-context seam
  before falling back to the broader refreshed-document scan boundary;
  that wrapper-level seam reuse and fallback boundary both read directly
  through the live with-context seam plus the remaining broader refreshed-
  document-scan generalization wording;
- broader vector/hybrid page/window orchestration has an explicit
  first narrowing at the top-level wrapper boundary: the remaining aggregation
  and reduce wrappers that need page/window hit material switch to
  dedicated `search_hits_page_for_query_vector_or_hybrid(...)` /
  `search_hits_window_for_query_vector_or_hybrid(...)` paths for
  vector-scored queries before dropping to the broader generic native
  page/window paths, with the remaining broader orchestration backlog
  sitting above that boundary;
- that wrapper-level split is surfaced through explicit
  `search_hits_page_for_query_index_aware(...)` /
  `search_hits_window_for_query_index_aware(...)` siblings, so several

single-index/multi-index `size=0` ownership splits and the local generic /

caller-owned vector/hybrid context propagation and higher distributed-reduce
generalization rather than another round of local wrapper extraction.

  its own exact-document and `MatchAll` background-document fallback directly

### 4. Broader hybrid bool generalization is still incomplete

Current state:

- lexical filtering can run natively;
- vector retrieval and fusion are still handled outside a fully native Tantivy
  pipeline;
- the common `bool` pattern with a single `should(knn)` clause and lexical
  `must/filter/must_not` constraints now uses a dedicated direct fusion path
  over vector candidates instead of rescoring every refreshed document;
- that direct fusion path now also preserves lexical-only candidates when the
  same `bool` query mixes a single `should(knn)` clause with additional lexical
  `should` clauses;
- the same candidate-reduction path now also covers multiple `should(knn)`
  clauses, combining vector candidate unions with lexical native candidates
  before final bool scoring;
- `minimum_should_match` values above `1` now also narrow candidate sets by
  actual per-clause match counts instead of treating all `should` candidates as
  a simple union, including representative nested `minimum_should_match > 1`
  request shapes with explicit-sort, `size=0`, and `top_hits` aggregation
  evidence, including representative `should`-, `must`-, `filter`-, and
  positive-candidate `must_not`-placement variants, with direct explicit-sort
  evidence on the `should`, `must`, `filter`, and positive-candidate
  `must_not` seats and direct `size=0` + `top_hits` evidence on the `should`,
  `must`, `filter`, and positive-candidate `must_not` seats too;
- that means the current representative placement matrix for nested hybrid
  `minimum_should_match > 1` shapes is no longer the main open seat; the
  remaining question is the broader generalized orchestration family beyond
  that matrix, whose representative seats now already carry both direct
  explicit-sort and direct `size=0` + `top_hits` evidence across the
  representative `should` / `must` / `filter` / positive-candidate
  `must_not` placements
- the current repo-local evidence stack now also includes a representative
  double-nested `minimum_should_match > 1` hybrid-bool `size=0` + `top_hits`
  request shape plus a representative explicit-sort result-path shape, so the
  remaining hybrid-bool question should not be framed as one more obvious
  deeper-nesting representative seat without first surfacing a broader
  orchestration/direct-path escape
- `bool` queries whose `should(knn)` clauses are optional
  (`minimum_should_match = 0`) can now also stay on the reduced path by
  starting from the refreshed local document universe instead of forcing an
  early scan escape, and no longer forces immediate fallback when there is no
  positive `must`/`filter` source;
- `bool` queries that place `knn` inside `must` or `filter` clauses now also
  use a candidate-reduced path by intersecting required vector candidates with
  lexical-native candidates before final bool scoring;
- those direct hybrid paths now remain active even when the top-level search
  request applies native sortable fields, with sort applied after candidate
  reduction instead of forcing a full fallback scan;
- `bool` queries with `knn` inside `must_not` can also stay on the direct path
  when there is a positive lexical or vector candidate source to exclude from,
  rather than forcing an immediate fallback;
- `bool` queries whose only positive semantics is `must_not(knn)` can now also
  stay on a bounded direct path by starting from the refreshed local document
  universe and excluding the matched vector candidates before final bool
  scoring;
- nested `bool` subtrees that contain these same `knn` placements now also use
  recursive candidate reduction before final bool scoring;
- non-vector lexical leaves that do not build a native Tantivy query
  (for example compatibility `wildcard` / `prefix` / `exists` leaves) now also
  contribute candidate ids through compatibility matching instead of forcing an
  immediate fallback when they appear inside those hybrid bool shapes;
- case-sensitive `prefix` and `wildcard` leaves can now build native Tantivy
  regex queries directly, so those hybrid bool shapes no longer need
  compatibility candidate scans for that subset of lexical leaves;
- `exists` leaves targeting scalar native field families (`keyword`, `i64`,
  `f64`, `bool`, and `date`) can now also build native Tantivy queries
  directly, so hybrid bool shapes that use those existence checks avoid
  another compatibility candidate-scan case;
- broader hybrid `bool` patterns outside these representative shapes still
  score documents through the general bool-query orchestration path rather
  than a dedicated native fusion collector.

Representative keyword/text `prefix` / `wildcard` hybrid fixtures now also pin
the vector-native paginated fetch phase directly for current unsorted / explicit
`_score desc` shapes, instead of only checking returned ids.

Impact:

- broader hybrid workloads still pay orchestration and compatibility-layer
  overhead;
- representative lexical-plus-vector hybrid queries now avoid some full-document
  rescoring overhead;
- mixed lexical-should plus single-`knn` hybrid queries also avoid dropping
  lexical-only matches while still reducing candidate work;
- multiple-`knn` should queries now reduce candidates before final bool scoring
  instead of scanning every refreshed document;
- the remaining hybrid gap is increasingly about broader shape generalization
  and fusion/reduce orchestration rather than the current representative
  lexical-plus-vector leaf set.
- pure `knn` and direct-path hybrid requests should now pay less top-level page
  orchestration overhead than before, even though broader vector execution is
  still not fully Tantivy-native.
- single-index vector and direct-path hybrid searches with native aggregation
  families now also avoid the generic full-hit aggregation path;
- multi-index vector requests with mergeable native aggregations now also avoid
  the generic all-hit aggregation path, but broader distributed vector reduce
  and non-mergeable aggregation combinations still fall back.

### 5. Broader search-hit materialization and response shaping overhead remains
above the engine core

Current state:

- even when query execution is native, Steelsearch still performs broader
  `SearchHit` materialization and compatibility JSON shaping above the Tantivy
  collector layer for returned search hits and for native paths that still
  need fetch-style payloads such as `top_hits`;
- current lexical/vector/hybrid page and page+aggregation fast paths now build
  only the requested page window instead of full match sets first, covering
  single-index lexical `match_all`, ordinary paginated lexical native-agg
  queries, and current pure `knn` / direct-path hybrid paginated requests;
- current compatibility/fallback-backed `size=0` paths now skip top-level hit
  materialization for representative single-index and multi-index
  lexical/vector/hybrid no-aggregation and no-`top_hits` aggregation shapes,
  including current text case-insensitive wildcard compatibility paths and
  current compatibility `significant_terms` shapes that still need background
  `match_all` document scans,
  plus representative script-sorted text case-insensitive wildcard
  `terms(service)` compatibility shapes;
- pure `knn` searches with explicit sort keys now also avoid cloning the full
  cached hit vector on request-result cache hits, keeping only the requested
  sorted page window during compatibility sorting on that cache-hit path;
- pure and hybrid multi-index vector searches now reuse the same per-index
  request-result cache before native reduce, preserving index-local refresh
  invalidation while exposing request-result cache detail entries per index;
- current native `top_hits` paths now keep only the requested `from + size`
  window instead of materializing full hit lists first, and current doc-backed
  vector/native aggregation collection avoids full `SearchHit`
  materialization entirely;
- when a single-index vector/native aggregation request only needs `top_hits`
  or finalize-only families on top of already-native inputs, it now also skips
  the otherwise redundant document-set scan for shard-local base collection;
- when a single-index vector-native page+aggregation request already fetches the
  default-score prefix up through `from + size` and that prefix covers the
  needed `top_hits` merge window, it now reuses that fetched prefix instead of
  issuing a second local `top_hits` window fetch, including the current
  explicit `_score desc` default-relevance sort shape;
- the same page-result reuse now also applies to the current single-index
  lexical native page+aggregation fetch under the same default-score
  prefix-window condition, including the current explicit `_score desc`
  default-relevance sort shape;
- for single-index lexical native aggregation requests whose shard-local base
  native family is empty after removing `top_hits` and finalize-only work, the
  engine now also skips redundant Tantivy query/searcher setup before building
  those late-stage results;
- for vector/native aggregation collection, Steelsearch now also skips
  `MatchAll` background-hit materialization unless the requested aggregation
  family actually needs it, which currently narrows that extra full-hit fetch
  to `significant_terms` and plugin-defined `significant_terms`.

Impact:

- lexical, sorted, and facet workloads remain close together in latency because
  shared top-of-pipeline overhead is still large;
- single-index lexical searches should now pay less hit materialization
  overhead than before, but vector, hybrid, multi-index fallback, and
  fetch-heavy paths still retain broader compatibility-layer cost;
- removing this overhead is likely more important than adding more isolated
  native query rewrites.

  before truncation;
- the same bounded local-window behavior now also covers explicit compatibility
  sort on pure `knn` shard-local windows instead of building the full local hit
  list before sort/truncation;

  ordering and covers the needed `top_hits` merge window, the current lexical
  and vector/hybrid page+aggregation reduce paths now reuse that shard-local
  page result instead of issuing a second shard-local rewrite fetch, including
  the current explicit `_score desc` default-relevance sort shape;

  `top_hits` aggregation collection and other finalize-only shard-local
  aggregation collection, relying on the bounded rewrite window and final
  reduce/finalize step instead;

  paths now also skip shard-local native reduce hint collection and empty
  aggregation collection entirely;
- per-index native reduce hint collection for `avg` / `weighted_avg`,
  `cardinality`, `percentiles` / `percentile_ranks` /
  `median_absolute_deviation` / `boxplot` now reuses a single native document
  fetch/scan instead of collecting those hint families through separate
  document passes;

  aggregation subset can now do native per-index collect plus native reduce
  without top-level hit fetch;
- shard fan-out, general cross-index merge, vector-aware reduce, and
  cluster-level distributed merge are still handled by upper orchestration
  layers.

Impact:

- current native execution gains are still strongest for local query work, but
  the `size=0` multi-index aggregation path is no longer purely fallback;
- broader multi-node scale-out behavior still depends heavily on non-native
  merge and orchestration cost.

### 7. Sort compatibility is not complete even though tuple sort is now native

Currently native:

- multi-field tuple sort for fast-field-backed `keyword`, `i64`, `f64`, and
  `bool`, and `date` fields;
- baseline missing-field ordering is covered for ascending and descending sorts
  on native fast-field paths;
- `unmapped_type` is natively honored for scalar fast-field families
  (`keyword`, integer/float families, `bool`, and `date`) so a missing sort
  field can stay on the native collector path instead of forcing a fallback;
- unmapped sort fields are verified to fall back cleanly to compatibility-layer
  ordering, allowing later mapped sort keys to continue determining result
  order;
- source-backed geo-distance sort is now supported on the compatibility sort
  path for `geo_point` fields.
- source-backed `geo_distance` query evaluation is now supported on the
  compatibility/native document-scan path for `geo_point` fields.
- `regexp` query evaluation is now supported on the `_id` / `keyword` /
  `text` query surface, including representative grouped hybrid bool direct
  candidate-reduction and native-helper evidence.

  `keyword` / `text` query surface, including representative grouped hybrid
  bool direct candidate-reduction and native-helper evidence.

  / `keyword` / `text` query surface, including representative grouped hybrid

In compact form, the remaining order is:

1. `distributed reduce`: broader cross-index/shard orchestration breadth
2. `hybrid bool`: broader nested/generalized compatibility breadth
3. `response/materialization`: broader hit-fetch-elision/orchestration breadth
   This compact remaining order is explicit in the current shape.
4. narrower semantic tail: current presence-oriented `exists` follow-on, with
   concrete note chain at
   `docs/rust-port/exists-semantics-follow-on.md`
   ->
   `docs/rust-port/exists-semantics-deeper-contract-check.md`

At the current state, these are best seen as broader follow-on implementation
themes rather than representative-family blockers.
They therefore sit closer to a future-breadth/generalization backlog than to a
short list of already-isolated missing representatives.

After those three workstreams, the remaining items are broader
coverage-breadth work rather than the primary residual blockers:

coverage already use Tantivy-native execution. The remaining native-gap work is
dominated by three broader backlog classes rather than specific
known representative-family holes, and sits together with the
future breadth/generalization backlog above:

longer reopens that same shared hit-context wrapper once inside its direct

requested-page-aggregation response-inputs-to-response-plus-reusable helper

Taken together, that top-level branch stands as
direct page plan
-> direct page-sibling fetch
-> direct fetched-page aggregation-context build
-> first page-top-hits try
-> later direct from-page branches
-> direct optional-reusable producer handoff.

- fallback highlight collection now also covers `regexp` and `fuzzy` leaves on both `_id` and non-`_id` seats, so those pattern families no longer silently fall through to no snippet output even when their explanation/count surface already recognizes the hit.

- default relevance ordering, general hit-sort fallback, and hit-backed `top_metrics` tie-breaks now also use `(index, _id)` identity instead of `_id` alone, so multi-index score ties and equal sort-key ties remain deterministic even when different indices share the same document id.
- the matching sort-less `top_hits` reduce merge comparator now also uses `_index` before `_id`, so built-in/plugin `top_hits` merge windows no longer keep one last `_id`-only multi-index tie-break seat.

- fallback highlight for `match_phrase_prefix` / `match_bool_prefix` now also gates on their real token-prefix matcher and falls back to generic field snippets instead of requiring literal whole-query substring presence, so those tokenized prefix seats no longer lose highlight output on valid non-literal matches.

- tokenized multi-field fallback highlight (`combined_fields`, `multi_match`, `query_string`, `simple_query_string`) now also uses matcher-gated generic field snippets instead of literal whole-query substring highlighting, so valid cross-field/tokenized matches no longer lose snippet output merely because the raw query text is not present contiguously in one field value.
- single-field tokenized fallback highlight (`match`, `match_phrase`) now likewise gates on the real matcher and falls back to generic field snippets instead of literal substring highlighting, so tokenized/local-phrase seats no longer require raw query text contiguity to emit snippets.
- `knn` fallback highlight now also gates the whole branch on actual local `knn` admission instead of emitting vector-field snippets on mere vector-shape compatibility alone, so filter-miss hits no longer leak `knn` highlight output.
- fallback highlight for `bool` and delegate-wrapper family (`span_multi`, `field_masking_span`, `wrapper`, `constant_score`, `boosting`, `function_score`, `script_score`) now also gates child traversal on actual local outer admission instead of delegating unconditionally, so child snippets no longer leak from non-matching outer queries.
- native significant-terms collectors now also use `source_value_for_highlight_field(...)` instead of direct `source.get(field)` lookup, so dotted/nested field addressing works the same way in hit-backed and document-backed significant-terms collection as it already does in the surrounding matcher/evidence surfaces.
- native `terms` / `significant_terms` collectors now also treat scalar array fields as multi-value bucket sources instead of silently skipping non-scalar top-level arrays, counting each distinct scalar bucket value per hit/document so source-backed native collection better matches multi-value field semantics.
- native `range` / `ip_range` / `date_range` collectors now also expand scalar array field values instead of treating top-level arrays as non-values, so multi-value numeric/string/date bucket families no longer silently drop array-backed bucket candidates during native collection.
- native histogram collection now also expands scalar numeric arrays and counts buckets per document rather than dropping top-level arrays entirely, so multi-value numeric fields can contribute to native histogram buckets without overcounting duplicate same-bucket values inside one document.

- Extended native/plugin `weighted_avg` collection from representative-scalar-only behavior to position-wise zipped numeric value/weight streams via `weighted_numeric_source_pairs(...)`, and aligned reduce-hint admission to that same pair stream so multi-value numeric fields now participate coherently in `weighted_avg` as long as value/weight positions pair up.
